design_references.title: Fleet CPG Engine — Phase 0 (Baseline)
design_references.claim: home-assistant/core is the fourth Phase 0 repo — the 'one huge repo', and structurally the actual fleet shape: enormous base, small per-PR diffs. This is what the O(diff) thesis has to survive. It also tests whether the roughly linear LOC-to-wall-time/RSS scaling observed across fastapi/zod/excalidraw (21k to 173k LOC) holds two more orders of magnitude out, or breaks.

hypothesis: Full joern process wall time (JVM start, CPG open, golden-query execution, teardown) is lower when Joern reuses an existing workspace project with a warm OS page cache (variant warm) than when it opens the CPG for the first time with no existing workspace project (variant cold), for home-assistant/core's homeassistant/ package at a pinned revision. (Already rejected on three smaller repos across two languages; this run checks whether ~3M LOC — two orders of magnitude past the largest prior repo — changes the outcome.)
null_hypothesis: Warm-variant process wall time is not meaningfully lower than cold-variant process wall time; any difference is within repetition noise.
independent_variable: Workspace/page-cache state before the joern process starts (cold: no prior workspace project for this CPG; warm: workspace project and OS page cache already populated by the immediately preceding cold run). The CPG binary, source revision, and query set are held fixed.

environment.network_justification: Materializes the pinned home-assistant/core revision via a shallow (`--depth 1`) `git clone` from github.com — full history is ~850MB and irrelevant to a single pinned-revision snapshot. Joern is already installed locally; no repeat download.

variants.name: cold
variants.description: Fresh workspace: no prior joern project for this CPG, unwarmed OS page cache for the CPG's on-disk representation.

variants.name: warm
variants.description: Reused workspace: joern project from the immediately preceding cold run still present, OS page cache warm.

metrics.acceptance_rule: Accept: median warm process_wall_time_ms is at least 20% lower than median cold process_wall_time_ms, across all 3 repetitions. Reject: the two medians are within 20% of each other, or warm is higher. Either way, cold_build wall time and peak RSS from cold_build.log are reported as the Phase 0 baseline deliverable, independent of this hypothesis's outcome. Additionally: report whether cold_build_wall_time_ms and peak_rss scale linearly with LOC relative to the fastapi/zod/excalidraw data points, or depart from that line.

evaluator.rubric: Score each query row on: (1) status == "ok" for every query in the golden set — any "error:*" status is a hard failure of the benchmark, not a data point to average away; (2) result_count is stable across all repetitions of the same (query_id, variant) pair for a fixed source revision — a changing count indicates the CPG itself is nondeterministic and invalidates the run (fleet-cpg-baseline-excalidraw already found one such case at ~173k LOC; check whether it recurs or worsens at ~3M); (3) compare median process_wall_time_ms for variant=warm against variant=cold across repetitions per the acceptance rule in metrics.acceptance_rule; (4) report cold_build wall time and peak RSS from cold_build.log as baseline numbers regardless of the cold/warm outcome.
